response.title: Württemberg
response.extract: Württemberg is a historical German territory in the south-west of present-day Baden-Württemberg, ruled as a county, then a duchy, and from 1806 to 1918 as the Kingdom of Württemberg with its capital at Stuttgart. For genealogists it is one of the better-documented German states: Lutheran and Catholic Kirchenbücher survive from the mid-1500s in many parishes, and the Familienregister — a household-by-household register unique to Württemberg and neighbouring Baden — consolidates a family's births, marriages and deaths onto a single page, often across three generations. Civil registration through the Standesamt began in 1876 following unification into the German Empire. Nineteenth-century emigration was heavy, driven by partible inheritance, the famine years of 1816-1817 and 1846-1847, and compulsory military service; departing families required an official release from citizenship, and the resulting Auswanderungsakten are held at the Staatsarchiv Ludwigsburg and often name every household member with an intended destination.
